content.user_title: Build Reusable Terraform Modules for AWS
content.value_statement: AWS Terraform modules can become inconsistent, fragile, and difficult to review. This skill provides focused patterns for reusable modules, remote state, validation, and stable resources.
actual_capabilities: Structures reusable modules with variables, outputs, resources, and version constraints.
Defines typed inputs and useful outputs for AWS resources.
Guides encrypted S3 remote state with DynamoDB locking.
Recommends stable resource identity through for_each.
Reviews HCL for formatting, validation, tagging, and version pinning.
Explains cautious recovery from stale Terraform state locks.
limitations: Covers Terraform on AWS, not CDK, CloudFormation, or other cloud providers.
Provides patterns and examples, not environment-specific validation or approval.
Does not inspect live AWS accounts or execute Terraform operations.
Remote state examples use placeholder names and require existing backend resources.

use_cases.title: Create Standard Modules
use_cases.description: Design reusable AWS modules with typed inputs, outputs, tags, and pinned dependencies.

use_cases.title: Review Terraform Changes
use_cases.description: Evaluate module structure, resource identity, validation, state handling, and maintainability before merging.

use_cases.title: Plan Terraform Migration
use_cases.description: Translate existing AWS infrastructure requirements into reusable Terraform module boundaries and state strategies.

prompt_templates.title: Create a VPC Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reusable Terraform module for an AWS VPC with typed variables, outputs, provider constraints, tags, and a short usage example.

prompt_templates.title: Review Module Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this AWS Terraform module for structure, version pinning, stable resource identity, validation, outputs, tags, and state exposure risks.

prompt_templates.title: Design Remote State
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an encrypted S3 backend and DynamoDB locking strategy for development, staging, and production, including isolation and recovery procedures.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a phased migration from manually managed AWS resources to Terraform modules, covering imports, state boundaries, dependencies, review gates, and rollback.

output_examples.input: Design a reusable VPC module for three availability zones.
output: A module layout with dedicated variable, resource, output, and version files.
Typed inputs for name, CIDR, and availability zones.
Outputs for the VPC identifier and integration points.

output_examples.input: Review a module that creates repeated subnets with count.
output: A review noting identity risks when list ordering changes.
A recommendation to use for_each with stable keys.
Validation steps using formatting and planning before merge.

output_examples.input: Propose remote state for a production team.
output: An encrypted S3 backend with isolated state keys.
A DynamoDB locking approach and access-control considerations.

best_practices: Pin provider and module versions before sharing modules.
Review Terraform plan output and validate configuration before merging.
Encrypt remote state, enable locking, and restrict backend access.
anti_patterns: Do not commit Terraform state files to version control.
Do not use count when resource identity must remain stable.
Do not force-unlock state before confirming that no operation is active.

faq.question: Can this skill execute Terraform commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples but does not run Terraform or access AWS.

faq.question: Which cloud provider does it cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on AWS resources managed with Terraform.

faq.question: Does it support remote state design?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers encrypted S3 state and DynamoDB locking for team environments.

faq.question: Can it review existing Terraform modules?
faq.answer: Yes. It can assess structure, versioning, resource identity, tags, outputs, and validation practices.

faq.question: Does it replace an infrastructure security review?
faq.answer: No. Validate every recommendation against your architecture, policies, permissions, and deployment environment.

faq.question: When should I avoid this skill?
faq.answer: Use another skill for AWS CDK, CloudFormation, or infrastructure outside AWS.
